sections.body: Window covered: the trading week ending 2026-09-04 (America/New_York), with same-instant snapshots as of 2026-09-08T00:11:43Z. This was a quiet, low-conviction close to the week, and the data supporting it is thin — the price-bar layer failed wholesale (every ETF and single-name bar request returned 502 Bad Gateway), so sector rotation, theme excess and weekly member returns are all untested this week. What can be said rests on the rates, vol, credit, dealer and policy layers, which did return. ## The macro backdrop is a Fed that markets lean toward hiking The cleanest signal is the policy path: the 9/16 FOMC carries a 57.9% HIKE probability as of 2026-09-07, from a prior band of 3.75-4.00%. That is corroborated outside our own feed — an Unusual Whales headline timestamped 2026-09-08T00:03:48Z notes 'markets price ~60% odds of a Fed hike next week.' A tightening-leaning Fed is consistent with the front end holding firm: DGS2 sits at 4.375 (essentially unchanged, +0 bp), while the 10-year (DGS10) is 4.79, +1 bp on the latest snapshot. The 2s10s curve at 41.5 is positive but the frame carries no prior observation for it, so I cannot characterise a weekly steepening or flattening — treat the level as a level, not a move. ## Risk appetite stayed benign despite the hike lean Credit and volatility both argue against stress. High-yield spreads (BAMLH0A0HYM2) are 2.65, in one notch from 2.66 as of 2026-09-03 — tight, and tightening at the margin. VIX (VIXCLS) is 14.52, up a fifth of a point (+0.21) from 14.31. A market pricing a coin-flip-plus rate hike while spreads compress and vol stays sub-15 is the signature of a soft, orderly tape rather than a defensive one; the judgement here is that the hike is largely digested, not feared.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.body:
Next week turns on the 9/16 FOMC, which sits just beyond the coming seven days but frames everything in front of it. Markets lean to a hike (57.9% as of 2026-09-07, ~60% per the 2026-09-08 headline), so the live question is whether that lean firms or fades. The observable that confirms a hike getting priced fully is the front end: watch DGS2 push above 4.375 and the 9/16 probability climb toward the high 60s. The observable that would invalidate the hike read is a soft US CPI (the same headline flags CPI as the near-term cap) pulling the probability back under 50 and letting the two-year ease.

What could persist: the benign risk backdrop. Sub-15 VIX and 2.65 high-yield spreads say the hike is digested, not feared. That holds as long as spreads stay inside ~2.70 and VIX stays under, say, the high-teens; a spread widening through 2.75-2.80 or a VIX break above 18 would be the first sign the orderly tape is breaking, and is the reverse risk to a complacent read. The gamma-flip structure (spot above 768.35) argues for contained moves near current levels, but that is a positioning statement that reverses if spot loses the flip — below it, hedging flows can amplify rather than dampen.

The single-name event that lands inside the week is ADBE earnings post-close 2026-09-10, implied move 6.9333%, IV rank 68.84 — elevated IV that reflects a real near-dated catalyst rather than distance, so a print in either direction should compress vol hard. I hold no directional view into it.

The large caveat: the price-bar layer failed this week, so I enter next week blind on sector rotation and on the el-nino-ag theme. Restoring bars is itself the first thing to watch — until XLK/XLF/XLE and the semis baskets return, any rotation narrative is untested, and I will not upgrade last week's leadership assumptions into facts. If bars return and semis or software lead into the ADBE print and the Fed, that is the confirmation to look for; if they return flat-to-defensive, the benign read is on notice.
